title: Easy Homemade Dill Pickles
description: Cool, crunchy, tangy refrigerator dill pickles made from scratch.
equipment: pint jars with lids and rings

steps: Wash and dry the jars and lids, and the cucumbers. Trim off the blossom or stem end of each cucumber; it has enzymes that can make pickles limp. Leave the cucumbers whole, cut them lengthwise into spears, or slice them crosswise into coins.
Divide the garlic, dill seeds and red pepper flakes (if using) evenly between the jars.
Pack the cucumbers into the jars as tightly as you can without smashing them (standing up if they're whole or in spears). Trim the ends if they come within ½ inch (1 cm) of the top of the jar.
Bring the vinegar, water and salt to a boil in a small saucepan over high heat. Pour the brine over the cucumbers, filling each jar to within ½ inch (1 cm) of the top. You may not need all of it.
Tap the jars gently on the counter a few times to release air bubbles, and top off with more brine if needed. Put on the lids and screw on the rings until tight, but not too tight.
Let the jars cool to room temperature, then refrigerate. The flavor improves as they age; try to wait at least 48 hours before opening.
